`vdf.jsonl` is generated by `tools/generate_vdf_fixtures.py` against mmx-node
`ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`. The oracle links the existing native
libraries, extracts Node::verify_vdf admission checks, verify_vdf_cpu,
find_vdf_points, ancestor lookups and space/header verification methods. Class
qualifiers change to the harness type. Only asynchronous admission scheduling
and trust bookkeeping are removed; every admission check remains. The reference
source and databases are untouched. Shared params/history snapshots use `seed`
references to earlier named rows.

205 proof rows compare original ProofOfTime hashes, exact WriteBytes preimages,
content hashes, validity, authentication, admission, output/end iteration helpers
and CPU verification. The oracle runs both native hardware dispatch and a second
copy with its two CPU feature flags disabled to reach the original fallback.
OpenMP chunk scheduling runs serially in this small harness for reproducible
diagnostics. Production native parallel execution may report a different invalid
segment when several fail; acceptance/rejection is unchanged.

Segment counts are 0, 1, 2, 15, 16, 17, 18, 32 and 34; segment sizes include zero,
1, 2, 3, 7, 31 and the production default of 50,000. Cases corrupt first/middle/last
segments, change mixed inputs, test shape/admission failures and signature errors,
wrap signed start metadata,
omit infused/difficulty ancestors, clamp commit delays at genesis and wrap the
iteration-count multiplication. Every row also compares original VDF_Point hashing
with embedded proof/receive-time data
that native hashing ignores. Rust constructs VerifiedPoint only after admission
and CPU verification both pass.

184 linkage rows exercise one/two/four-point chains, delayed infusions and
committed time difficulties, skipped ancestor VDF heights, absent outputs/parents,
missing points, count mismatch, pool ordering and duplicate outputs with different
signed metadata. Points are independently admitted and CPU-verified first. Native
find_vdf_points ignores signed start/height metadata and does not compare the
block's reward vector with point reward addresses. Fixtures deliberately keep
these exemptions observable instead of tightening native consensus rules.

63 pipeline rows reuse the positive small-k8 space witnesses in `work.jsonl`.
They combine native header hashes/authentication, actual ancestor resolution,
verified VDF output chains and full space/header transition verification across
hardforks 1 and 2. They cover one/two/four-point blocks, missing/corrupt linkage,
iteration/weight/signature mutations and the native reward-vector exemption.
Rust additionally prepares/aborts/commits empty body settlement and rejects a
different ledger parent. Generating these rows requires the checked-in work
fixture; they do not construct production-sized plots.

These fixtures do not implement timelord scheduling, VDF trust/sync shortcuts,
proposer peak selection, durable point/header archives or chain selection. The
supplied header source must represent authenticated history for the same chain
parameters used to verify the points.
